title: PostgreSQL 18: Constraints
excerpt: Primary, foreign-key, unique, not-null, check, and exclusion constraints encode data invariants in the database.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Indexes
excerpt: Indexes can accelerate row retrieval but add system overhead and must be chosen against real access patterns.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Using EXPLAIN
excerpt: EXPLAIN exposes the query plan selected by the planner so performance hypotheses can be tested against evidence.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Transaction Isolation
excerpt: Isolation levels define which concurrency phenomena may occur, with Serializable emulating a serial order for committed transactions.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Concurrency Control
excerpt: PostgreSQL concurrency control balances simultaneous access with data integrity through MVCC, locks, and retryable failures.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Modifying Tables
excerpt: ALTER TABLE supports deliberate schema evolution across columns, constraints, defaults, and types, each with operational consequences.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Row Security Policies
excerpt: Enabled row security restricts visible or modifiable rows by policy and defaults to deny when no policy allows access.

title: PostgreSQL 18: SQL Dump
excerpt: pg_dump creates internally consistent logical backups, but restoration must be exercised and verified as an independent operation.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery
excerpt: Base backups plus archived write-ahead log records support restoration to a selected recovery point.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Cumulative Statistics System
excerpt: PostgreSQL statistics views expose activity and accumulated behavior needed for query and incident diagnosis.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Materialized Views
excerpt: Materialized views persist query results for faster reads but require explicit refresh and may not contain current data.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Logical Replication
excerpt: Logical replication publishes data changes to subscribers and supports incremental movement into read and analytics systems.

title: SQL As Understood By SQLite
excerpt: SQLite implements most SQL while documenting supported syntax and engine-specific omissions or extensions.

title: SQLite Transaction Control
excerpt: SQLite supports explicit BEGIN, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK semantics and distinguishes read from write transactions.

title: SQLite Foreign Key Support
excerpt: SQLite foreign-key constraints maintain parent-child integrity when support is enabled and correctly indexed.

title: SQLite Query Planning
excerpt: SQLite uses a cost-based planner to choose among access paths, including multi-column and covering indexes and indexed sorting.
